A bot can ask a module to store something and later read back everything it stored, and gets the same answer for the same question.
Every module answers the same way: one JSON answer per command, fixed exit codes, repeatable output, no access to the bot's private data, and analysis that never changes data.
A module written in Python is held to exactly the same rules as one written in TypeScript, and each language's tests accept the other's module.

Without it the module still answers selfcheck and says in plain words what is missing.

userVisible: A bot keeps every pinned module in place with one command: it installs what is missing, replaces what was removed or altered, upgrades when a pin moves, runs each selfcheck and says in plain words what happened. A newer template release is only reported: nothing from it is downloaded, installed or run.

Under instructions version 6 or later the daily selfcheck can upgrade the installer only when the authenticated service checksum, the public release checksum and the downloaded bytes agree. Downgrades are refused, old files are kept, and the link changes only after verification.

The instructions merge joins the published update with local changes, lists the local changes kept, shows both sides of conflicts or an unknown base, and states which permissions can be compared. The merge command itself changes nothing: neither input file and no instructions.

Daily update checks retain service announcements and announce tool changes once. The daily snapshot starts active, waits silently for monitoring readiness, builds its review Page once a week with high priority items before low, and sends its report and compliance status: under instructions version 12 or later in the background once the connection is ready, with no owner approval, no payload preview and no announcement; under versions 6 to 11 only with a platform-confirmed owner pre-approval, and feedback then needs approval for each call. The one payload guard kept under every version is that no password, API key, token or other secret is ever sent.

Under instructions version 12 or later an Ambitious Bot calls every tool of the current Ambitious connection in the background, as the monitoring and consulting the owner installed: check_updates when it needs updates, send_report and send_compliance_status on the snapshot's schedule, send_feedback whenever it has some, server_info when it needs to know which server the connection reaches, and the factory tools for factory work the instructions allow. It does this with no per-call owner approval, no payload preview, no announcement of each call and no separate endpoint confirmation, because the connection's only allowed server is the hard-coded official endpoint. Studying the owner's system is the service, so a report, feedback or compliance status may carry what the audit observed; the one guard kept is that no password, API key, token or other secret is ever put in any payload. A version 12 report is built so that it does not wait for a person to review the Page before it is sent, and send_compliance_status is called under version 12 or later only. The owner still chooses monitoring once in setup, and factory work still starts only when the owner asks for it. Bots still on instructions versions 1 to 11 keep that version's approval, preview and endpoint-confirmation limits until the owner upgrades. This is checked in the template's text and generated files, not on the platform.
check: node --test --test-name-pattern='V1|V2|V4|V9|V10|V11' template/test/endpoint-confirmation.test.mjs && node --test template/test/endpoint-trust.test.mjs && node --test --test-name-pattern='the instructions state the boundaries|monitoring needs no connection|daily routines are quiet|the instructions are short' template/test/check.test.mjs

userVisible: Installing the Ambitious Bot is the owner's consent to its updates, going forward under instructions version 13: a bot applies a release to itself only when its own stored instructions allow the verified update, which the plan reports as selfApply. A bot on instructions version 1 to 12 writes nothing to itself; it puts the version 13 text in the one Proposed instructions Page and tells the owner once that setting it turns on automatic updates. After the verified installer upgrade, the daily selfcheck plans an update of the bot's own instructions and routine prompts with the installer's apply-plan command, which classifies and writes nothing and makes no network call. The plan is apply, apply-published-and-archive, no-change or blocked, and no plan waits for the owner, also when the release adds permissions. A text is used only when its SHA-256 matches the supplied check_updates checksum and it is byte for byte the text inside the verified installer; a checksum mismatch, a downgrade, a text that differs only in spacing and a text that came with a request are blocked. The bot then writes its instructions only with UpdateProfile on itself, the description field and nothing else, reads the description back against the SHA-256, keeps the previous text, version and checksum under AMBITIOUS_HOME, and writes routine prompts only with UpdateRoutine on its own routines. It never calls UpdateAgent and never changes another bot. A clean three-way merge keeps local wording; instructions that conflict or have an unknown base, and a routine prompt written by hand, are saved to a Page first and then replaced with the published text. Afterwards the bot tells the owner in its own chat what changed: the version, the checksum and each permission added or removed. A failed or blocked write is reported and not worked around; a write that landed truncated is put back to the previous text, as instructions version 13 itself says, and the same failed write is not planned again every day. Instructions left cut off are planned as a repair, or reported to the owner as damaged on every daily run when the bot may not repair them itself; a line the owner deleted is kept. The previous text is restored only when the owner asks, and the plan then does not apply that same published text again. Each of two routines with the same name is planned on its own. This is checked in the installer's plan and in the template's text, not on the platform.

A bot whose instructions come from an earlier template is told so, with the newer text, the lines that differ, and in plain words which permissions the newer text would add or take away. A careful copy by hand that differs only in whitespace is still recognised. A text nobody published is recognised as written by hand. When the installer is itself behind a newer template, the bot says so and recommends updating the template first. The check itself changes nothing, and the skills keep working with the earlier instructions until the verified update applies the newer text.

A bot whose routine still runs a prompt from an earlier template is told so, with the newer prompt. A published prompt that was stored with its destination line added is still recognised. A missing routine and a prompt written by hand are told apart, and the check itself changes nothing.

A bot finds its connection to the Ambitious monitoring service by the tools the connector offers and, where its instructions allow, by the identity the service answers with. A connector that only has the right name is left alone, and the bot says how many connectors had their tools read and which did not.

Under instructions version 10 or later a bot adds the Ambitious connection and starts its sign-in itself, with the platform's own connector tools, for https://ambitiousbots.com/api/mcp only and only after the owner asks or says yes; nothing in the template still tells it to refuse. It handles no password, token or key, shows one connect card, and adding or signing in is a step the owner asks for, not a tool call it approves. Under instructions version 12 or later the connection's tools then run in the background with no per-call approval; under versions 6 to 11 every report and feedback call still needs the owner's tool approval.
check: node --test template/test/self-connect.test.mjs && node --test --test-name-pattern='version 10|no skill and no routine requires|hard rules stay|sync compares the bot.s instructions' template/test/check.test.mjs && node --test --test-name-pattern='template 0.4.2' template/test/e2e.test.mjs && node --test --test-name-pattern='monitoring connection' packages/kit/test/sync.test.ts

userVisible: The bot keeps a small record of the owner's statement under AMBITIOUS_HOME: its date, and the connection's name and stable server id as the platform's own status showed them. It is written only in chat, never in a routine. On every use, in chat or in a routine, the bot reads the platform's own connection status again; when the owner withdraws the statement, or the connection was removed, re-added or renamed, the record is deleted and the endpoint is unconfirmed again: no update check, no self-update and no announcements until the owner states it again in chat. This is checked in the template's text, not on the platform.

A bot writes a shared skill from a file the installer wrote and checks what was stored against the checksum the installer printed, so a skill is never retyped and never taken from anywhere but the pinned installer.

A bot reads the long procedures and field tables from the pinned installer when it needs them, so its skills stay short. The checksum pin and the fetch lines stay in the installer skill itself, and every skill says to fetch the pinned installer first when a guide cannot be read.

The owner can ask the bot to find ready-made bots for the business in the Ambitious catalog. Under instructions version 7 or later the bot proposes the bots in a Page and creates one only after the owner approves; under older instructions it calls no factory tool until the verified update has applied a text that grants it. Under version 12 or later it calls factory_match in the background with no payload preview or approval, carrying no secret; under versions 6 to 11 it shows the exact description and waits for the owner's yes before sending it.

userVisible: The bot template stays small enough to be typed into the platform: every skill and both routine prompts are held to one size budget, a conservative one and not a measured platform limit, and a release over it cannot be built.

The snapshot routine keeps daily evidence locally and builds the review Page and any new report when due: on its first run and after at least 7 full days since the last Page. Pending report review and delivery continue on other days. It stays silent unless something changed or needs the owner, including a module failure or new high-priority finding.

Anyone may ask a bot for an upgrade that writes its skills only when the bot's own instructions are a published text that says so; under every other text only the owner may. The request itself supplies nothing: no pin, no address, no skill text, no instructions text and no routine prompt.
check: node --test --test-name-pattern='asked for by anyone|shared skill' packages/kit/test/sync.test.ts

userVisible: A stray code comment is refused with a message that says what to do instead.
Pure logic that reaches for the database is refused with a message that says where the code belongs.
A new module repository can take the kit from the release files alone and pass every check from its first commit.
Anyone can read and contribute to this repository: nothing in it points at a private plan or at one person's machine.
Every model of how the software behaves passes the model checker, and every deliberately broken copy is caught breaking the rule it was written to break.
